text:
Samir Patel: quick intake — can we prioritize onboarding atlas-40b-quant for the generative-summaries workload? Sanity check: baseline perf looked promising in TPU tests but we need GPU quant results and a quality sweep. Will add a short checklist below.
Devon Li: +1 from infra side if GPU quant runs fit in our nightly slot. what's the expected token throughput?
Samir Patel: rough guess 250-350 tok/s on a single A100-80GB with int8 kernels, but that's speculative until we run end-to-end.
Maria Gonzales: request: please add the eval prompt set used for summarization (summaries-v2). we should run both ROUGE and human-flavored faithfulness checks. also need regression hooks vs current prod (redwood-13b-v2).
Chris Yao: where does this land on roadmap? Q2 capacity is tight — if this is medium priority we may defer to next cycle unless it shows clear latency/cost wins.
Samir Patel: roadmap note: PMs flagged potential 10–15% unit cost reduction for multi-doc summarization; that bumped it to medium-high. proposing canary in dedicated pool if quantized perf holds.
Nina R: infra question — do we use dedicated quant image or the runtime's new int8 kernels? I prefer testing both to compare memory and latency.
Samir Patel: checklist (copy/paste into runs):
```
- Pull model: atlas-40b HF repo + config
- Convert to our quant format (int8, per-channel) using quant-tool v0.9
- Nightly perf job (A100-80GB): 1k short prompts + 200 long prompts
- Run eval suite: summaries-v2 (rouge, bertscore, faithfulness), toxic-filter
- Regression diff vs redwood-13b-v2 using sample-set-2026-02
- Canary config: dedicated-small pool, autoscale off, fallback to atlas-40b-fp16
- Postmortem checklist: latency, cost, quality deltas
```
Devon Li: I'll reserve the nightly slot; tagging infra-bot to create the job.
infra-bot: Job request received: create-nightly-run atlas-40b-quant on a100-80gb. Queue position: 4.
Maria Gonzales: For human evals, who will coordinate? I can assemble the MTurk batch if we have finalized prompts.
Samir Patel: Maria — can you take lead on human evals? I'll own the quant conversion and perf runs.
Chris Yao: ok if it shows >=8% cost savings with <1.5% quality delta we fast-track to canary. otherwise deprioritize.
Nina R: quick note: include KV cache size tests for multi-doc flows — we've tripped OOMs before with similar models.
Devon Li: noted. I'll add memory/oom monitors to the job and set alert if >75% GPU mem usage.
Maria Gonzales: plan for timeline? trying to sync with PM roadmap call Thursday.
Samir Patel: timeline: quant conversion + perf runs by Wed, evals by Fri, human-run results next Tue. aggressive but doable if jobs start tonight.
Chris Yao: cool. if anything blocks, ping me and I'll escalate capacity.
Samir Patel: thanks all — will post updates as run logs appear. :eyes:
